query: What does Seun's self-description of her eating habits suggest about where she stood with her dietary identity at that point — and what in how she frames a particular moment reveals it?
gold: Seun was already holding herself to a vegan standard internally before she formally announced it. In Session 1 she describes eating fish over Christmas as a lapse she regrets ('I did eat more fish than I wanted') and immediately reasserts her plant-based identity ('I am back on strictly plant-based now'). The defensiveness — framing the fish as something that happened to her ('I only slipped') rather than a choice — signals that her self-concept had already shifted to fully plant-based, even if practice had not yet caught up. By Session 3 the health-check results gave her the external confirmation she needed to commit publicly and drop the apologetic framing.

Seun describes herself as “someone who thought veganism was oyinbo food last year.” That suggests her dietary identity at that point was that of a former skeptic: she had seen veganism as foreign and “white people’s food,” outside her own food culture — not as something she herself belonged to.

But the way she frames the moment reveals she has shifted and is now emotionally invested. She calls the moment “the most motherly thing” and “everything,” and she says, “this is what I mean when I say wellness is not about restriction it is about permission” when “Auntie Grace just gave herself permission.” The “coming from someone who thought veganism was oyinbo food last year” framing makes the contrast explicit: she is moved by a moment she would not have appreciated from her earlier, dismissive position. So she stood at that point as someone who once rejected veganism as alien but now identified with a permission-based, emotionally meaningful wellness identity rather than a restrictive one.
